name: Responsive Block Controls
author: Specia1ne

sections.description:
Adjust layouts, spacing, widths and heights for different screen sizes directly in the WordPress block sidebar. Responsive Block Controls extends native Gutenberg blocks without a page builder or replacement blocks.

Why use it?

  • Keep your native blocks, patterns and template parts.
  • Reuse desktop and responsive layouts with named presets.
  • Keep theme defaults unless you override them. Removing the plugin does not delete your content.

Supported blocks

  • Columns — columns per row, gaps and custom widths.
  • Column — width and order for each screen size, with Custom widths enabled on its parent.
  • Query Loop (Post Template grid) — columns, minimum column width, gaps and optional Masonry.
  • Gallery — columns and gaps.
  • Spacer — tablet and mobile heights.
  • Media & Text — side-by-side or stacked layouts, stacked order and media width.
  • Cover — minimum height for four tablet and mobile screen sizes.

How it works

Settings stay on native WordPress blocks. The plugin adds styles for supported layout properties; it does not add replacement blocks or extra content wrappers. Your theme provides defaults unless you override them with the controls or apply a preset.

Editor experience

  • Controls appear in the sidebar for supported blocks.
  • Most blocks offer four tablet and mobile breakpoints. Spacer uses Tablet and Mobile.
  • Gap, Cover height and Media & Text settings inherit wider values until overridden.
  • Plugin gap and height controls support px, rem and em.
  • Column width and order can be set separately for each breakpoint.
  • Media & Text retains saved widths when switching between stacked and side-by-side layouts.
  • Reset affects the current setting and breakpoint, not the whole block.

Layout presets

Save desktop and responsive layout settings once, then reuse them on compatible native blocks on any page. Preset controls are inside each block’s existing responsive panel.

  • Enable responsive controls, then choose Save as preset below the settings and enter a name. Spacer needs no mode switch. Presets are created by you, not supplied automatically.
  • The selector sits below the mode switch and shows presets for the current block type, even with the mode off. Choose one and click Apply; selection alone changes nothing.
  • Presets include supported desktop and responsive settings. Content, media, block structure and unrelated styles are kept. Apply supports Undo and leaves incompatible blocks unchanged.
  • The top actions menu offers copy, rename, update, delete and JSON import/export. Compatible blocks show Paste settings near the preset selector. These actions remain available with the mode off, except copying or updating from inactive controls.
  • Users allowed to edit theme settings can manage presets; other content editors can apply them. You can also apply a preset to multiple selected blocks from their options menu.
  • Applied settings are independent copies. Editing or deleting a preset does not update blocks that used it.

WordPress 7.1 responsive styles

WordPress 7.1 responsive settings and the plugin’s four-breakpoint settings are stored separately.

  • Enable “Use 4 breakpoints” for separate tablet landscape, tablet portrait, mobile landscape and mobile portrait settings. Leave it off to use WordPress behavior.
  • The editor warns about overlapping settings. Plugin columns and gaps take priority at its breakpoints. Custom Cover heights also override WordPress height and aspect ratio where set.
  • Switching back keeps both sets of values. Unrelated WordPress styles, such as typography and padding, continue to work.

Accessibility and localization

  • Inspector controls are keyboard accessible and labeled for screen readers.
  • Strings are translation-ready via the responsive-columns text domain.
sections.installation:
1. Install Responsive Block Controls from the WordPress plugin directory or upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Select a supported native block and open the responsive panel in the block sidebar.
sections.faq:
Is this a page builder or a block collection?

No. The plugin extends supported native Gutenberg blocks. It does not replace core blocks with custom layout blocks.

Which blocks are supported?

Columns, Column, Query Loop grids, Gallery, Spacer, Media & Text and Cover. See Supported blocks above for their controls.

Will my content break if I uninstall the plugin?

No. Settings are stored as extra block attributes. If the plugin is removed, WordPress ignores those attributes and the blocks fall back to their normal core behavior.

Does it work with patterns and reusable blocks?

Yes. Because settings are stored on native blocks, they travel with patterns, synced patterns, reusable blocks, and template parts.

Can I use it with any theme?

The plugin is designed to work with themes that use normal WordPress block markup and spacing styles. It keeps the active theme responsible for the base layout and only applies responsive overrides where supported.

Does Masonry work everywhere?

No. Masonry requires a Query Loop grid with at least two fixed desktop columns and no minimum column width.

Can I use rem or em values for gaps?

Yes. Gap controls support px, rem, and em values, while older saved px values remain compatible.

Can Spacer have different heights on tablet and mobile?

Yes. Keep the native desktop height in the Spacer block settings, then use the responsive height panel for tablet and mobile overrides.

What changes on a Media & Text block?

The responsive controls change only configured tablet/mobile layouts and their inherited narrower values. Choose side by side or stacked, stacked order and side-by-side media width. Saved widths are kept when stacked. These controls do not change desktop settings; applying a preset can.

How does responsive Cover height work?

Set desktop height in the WordPress block settings. Enable “Use 4 breakpoints” and set minimum heights as needed; narrower breakpoints inherit wider values. Custom heights override WordPress height and aspect ratio where set, but keep those values saved. Content can grow beyond the minimum height.

How does this work with WordPress 7.1 responsive styles?

With “Use 4 breakpoints” off, WordPress controls the layout. With it on, the plugin takes priority for supported settings at its breakpoints. Overlapping settings trigger a warning; switching back does not delete either set of values.

What does Reset change?

Reset affects only the current setting and breakpoint. Tablet/mobile gaps, Cover height and media width return to inherited values. Column counts return to their defaults. Desktop gap Reset restores theme spacing without clearing tablet/mobile gaps. Content and other settings are kept.

Does applying a preset change my content or desktop styles?

Presets change supported desktop and responsive layout settings, including widths, gaps and heights. They never copy content or media. Unset responsive values return to inheritance or defaults; unrelated styles and WordPress responsive values are kept.

Can changing a preset update all pages that use it?

No. Applied settings are independent snapshots. Reapply a preset explicitly to update selected blocks. Deleting a library preset does not delete block settings, and deactivating the plugin retains the library.

Can I apply a Columns preset to a different number of columns?

No. The number of Column blocks must match so each receives the correct widths and order. Presets never add or delete columns. Gallery and Query Loop change grid settings without requiring matching image or post counts, subject to their column limits.

How do I copy settings to another block?

Choose Copy layout settings, select another compatible block and click Paste settings. The copy lasts only within the current editor page; reloading or leaving clears it. Save a named preset to reuse settings on other pages.

Can I save an identical preset?

The plugin offers the existing preset or an explicit Save a copy with a unique name. It does not create accidental duplicates automatically.

How do import and export work?

Export downloads saved presets, not unsaved block changes. Import skips identical layouts, even with different names. Conflicting names can be skipped or imported with new names; existing presets are never overwritten by import.

Which settings are excluded from presets?

Content, media, query parameters, block structure, colors, typography and unrelated styles are excluded. Query Loop targets must already be grids. Unsupported values or theme spacing sizes missing on the target site cannot be applied.
sections.changelog:
2.0.0

  • Added site-wide presets to reuse desktop and responsive layouts on compatible blocks, including multiple selected blocks.
  • Added layout copy/paste, explicit duplicate handling and validated JSON import/export, with permission-protected storage, conflict confirmation and Undo for block changes.

1.9.0

  • Added opt-in four-breakpoint minimum height for Cover, with inheritance, scoped Reset, and guidance when native WordPress height or aspect-ratio settings overlap.
  • Added per-breakpoint media width for plugin-managed Side by side Media & Text layouts, preserving native width and saved values when layouts change.

1.8.0

  • Added responsive Media & Text layouts across four non-desktop breakpoints, with inherited, side-by-side, and stacked modes plus stacked media/text order.
  • Kept Media & Text desktop behavior, native media width, saved markup order, and native Stack on mobile setting unchanged.
  • Added an opt-in Advanced 4 breakpoints mode alongside WordPress 7.1 responsive styles, including overlap detection, conflict guidance, and reversible switching without deleting saved settings.
  • Scoped Reset actions: column count now returns only the active non-desktop value to its default; non-desktop spacing resumes inheritance; and desktop spacing restores the theme base without deleting non-desktop maps, overrides, or the independent row-gap setting.

1.7.4

  • Fixed Columns content safety and responsive Masonry spacing, availability, and dynamic relayout.
  • Updated editor compatibility and ensured bundled translations are included in release packages.

1.7.3

  • Confirmed compatibility with WordPress 7.0.

1.7.2

  • Improved responsive Spacer height validation in the editor so unsupported values are ignored and supported values stay within safe limits.
  • Improved responsive CSS value sanitization on the front end.

1.7.1

  • Renamed the plugin to Responsive Block Controls and refreshed its directory positioning, screenshots, and metadata.
  • Hardened responsive gap and minimum-width sanitization, including legacy runtime style handling.

1.7.0

  • Added responsive height controls and live tablet/mobile resizing for native Spacer blocks.
  • Improved deactivation-safe behavior so supported native blocks remain valid.

1.6.0

  • Added responsive column and gap controls for native Gallery blocks.
  • Improved Gallery editor previews for tablet and mobile breakpoints.

1.5.0

  • Added custom-width mode for native Columns layouts.
  • Added per-column responsive width and order controls for asymmetric layouts.

1.4.0

  • Added Query Loop grid support, including manual columns, auto-fit minimum width, and Masonry guardrails.

1.3.0

  • Added the shared breakpoint control panel, responsive gap inheritance, and bundled editor translations.

1.2.0

  • Improved CSS value sanitization, theme gap detection, editor preview targeting, and Masonry stability.

1.1.0

  • Reworked frontend HTML handling to use WP_HTML_Tag_Processor and improved asset loading fallbacks.

1.0.0

  • Initial public release.
